sections.title: Three concrete experiments
sections.summary: Run these before increasing build scope.

statements.text: Problem-frequency interviews: Interview 8 qualified Client-service agencies and service operations leaders; capture the last occurrence, current workaround, frequency, consequence, and owner. Success: At least 5 describe a recent occurrence and 3 actively seek a better workflow.
Concierge workflow pilot: Run the core workflow manually with 3 teams for 14 days; log repeated use, completion time, and abandonment. Success: At least 2 teams use it twice and ask to continue.

Paid-offer test: Present the same scoped offer to 5 qualified buyers and request payment, a deposit, or a signed paid-pilot commitment. Success: At least 2 buyers make a monetary or signed commitment.

sections.title: Final recommendation
sections.summary: Do not build beyond a cheap demand test. Founder action: recruit 8 qualified participants from The buyer or workflow owner at a qualified Client-service agencies and service operations leaders organization via Founder-led outreach through professional-service associations, agency directories, and warm introductions; screen for recent customer sign-off responsibility. Offer and artefact: Interview 8 qualified Client-service agencies and service operations leaders; capture the last occurrence, current workaround, frequency, consequence, and owner. Timing: 7 days. Success threshold: At least 5 describe a recent occurrence and 3 actively seek a better workflow. Failure threshold: Fewer than 3 report a recent, consequential occurrence. Decision unlocked: Whether the approval/sign-off problem is frequent and consequential enough to justify a workflow product.
